column3: {"ok":0,"reason":"At the starting throttle (575 K): the engine has no steady operating point: the compressors would have to run off the part of their maps the model covers. Mostly this is a throttle too low for the air (at the design flight, below about 510\u2013520 K on every map; warmer air raises that, and so does flying faster, which warms the air before it reaches the engine \u2014 about 610 K at Mach 1.6, 670\u2013690 K at Mach 2, 800\u2013820 K at Mach 2.6; colder air lowers it), or a large fixed load or amount of air in thin air, or a lever whose schedule does nearly all its travel just below the design speed. Move this throttle toward the middle of its range, or start the lever's schedule lower. (The model says: rung-91 two-shaft closure with turbine cooling does not bracket at nu=(0.0529,0.5576), Tt4=575, b=0.1000 \u2014 off the modeled speed-line region.) With the generator off this throttle does have a steady point, so the generator's load is what removes it: ask for less power, or raise the throttle."}
